definition: Splitting words into frequent fragments so any string can be represented with a bounded vocabulary: common words stay whole, rare words decompose.
details: Splitting words into frequent fragments so any string can be represented with a bounded vocabulary: common words stay whole, rare words decompose. The compromise between character-level (long sequences) and word-level (unbounded vocabulary) approaches.

explainer.lead: Subword tokenisation splits words into frequent fragments so any string can be represented with a bounded vocabulary. It matters as the compromise between character-level approaches, which give long sequences, and word-level approaches, which give an unbounded vocabulary.

tiers.eli5: It breaks unusual words into familiar pieces, like building a big word from smaller chunks you already know.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it so common words stay whole while rare words decompose, keeping the vocabulary bounded. A pitfall is that fragmentation choices affect how well rare or domain-specific terms are represented.
tiers.paperLevel: Splitting words into frequent fragments so any string can be represented with a bounded vocabulary: common words stay whole, rare words decompose.

explainer.example: A rare compound word is split into two frequent fragments that the model already knows, so no out-of-vocabulary token is needed.
